messages:
maria_support: Customer (Acme corp) reporting intermittent 502s and high tail latency after the canary rollout of redwood-v2.0.1. Seeing ~12-18% error rate on their traffic. Provided two request_ids: req_2026031701, req_2026031702. They want repro steps and guidance on pinning back to stable.
jasper_oncall: thanks — can you paste the exact request_id headers and a short curl sample they used? also which region and traffic routing (canary weight)?
deploy-bot: canary rollout started: redwood-v2.0.1 -> 10% traffic (us-west-2), triggered by emma. build: bld-20260317-47
ingrid_research: quick hypothesis: might be KV cache mismatch in v2.0.1 causing cache warm failures + extra latency; also check compilation kernel fallback logs (we saw that with quantized kernels before).
oliver_engineer: can we get a minimal curl reproducer from them. ask them to include x-request-id + model pin header. example we can give them:
```bash
curl -sS https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "x-request-id: repro-req-01" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-v2.0.1","input":"Summarize the following...","max_tokens":64}'
```
oliver_engineer: for pinning to stable for repro try: add header `x-model-pin: redwood-v1.9.8` or set `model: \"redwood-v1.9.8\"` in body — that forces stable fallback route.
emma_support: customer ran a simple batch of 200 calls, 10% failed with 502 and ~30% had latency >1.2s (normal ~120ms). region: us-west-2, canary weight: 10%.
jasper_oncall: emma — please request they run the curl above but set `-H "x-model-pin: redwood-v1.9.8"` and capture both failing and succeeding response headers. ask them to save raw responses and include the x-request-id as we need server logs.
maria_support: sent instructions to Acme; also requested debug bundle from their request origin. asked them to run the support debug endpoint: `POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/support/debug-bundle` with `x-request-id` list (we'll give them back a pre-signed upload link).
ingrid_research: when you get bundles, please include these logs from the client side: runtime.log (client SDK), network trace (curl -v), plus the server request_id mapping. check for these server log markers: `kernel_fallback`, `kv_cache_miss`, `batch_split`.
oliver_engineer: if they can't repro locally, we should try internal replay using the same request ids and model pin to reproduce latency on our side. ask infra to isolate those requests in traces.
maria_support: Acme uploaded two debug bundles (links posted privately). I pulled the trimmed server log snippet — here's the relevant lines: 
```
[2026-03-17T14:02:14Z] req=req_2026031701 model=redwood-v2.0.1 latency=128ms status=200 kernel_fallback=false
[2026-03-17T14:02:15Z] req=req_2026031702 model=redwood-v2.0.1 latency=1350ms status=502 kernel_fallback=true reason=kv_cache_missing
```
maria_support: uploaded the full bundles to support-bucket/sensitive/acme-17695 (permissioned).
jasper_oncall: ok that `kernel_fallback=true` + `kv_cache_missing` lines align with Ingrid's hypothesis. Oliver, can you reproduce with an internal run where we force kv cache cold start + 10% canary traffic?
oliver_engineer: I'll schedule a replay job. quick checklist for repro run: 1) set canary weight 10% in us-west-2, 2) push redwood-v2.0.1 build, 3) replay request set with the provided bodies and request-ids, 4) enable verbose kernel logs.
emma_support: customer is ok to be in maintenance window tomorrow 02:00-03:00 UTC for controlled repro. they asked if we can pin them back in the meantime.
jasper_oncall: yes we can pin them. maria — apply customer-level override to route their traffic to redwood-v1.9.8 and keep canary for others. do not rollback globally. add a note to the change that it's temporary and tied to ticket #TKT-4591.
maria_support: done — I applied customer pin and reduced canary weight for them to 0% (other customers unaffected). confirmed with a quick smoke check: their 50 sample calls now show ~0% errors and latencies back to ~110-140ms.
ingrid_research: thanks — once Oliver reproduces internally, let's compare kernel decision traces. if kv_cache logic is the culprit we might need a quick patch to v2 to avoid fallback on borderline misses.
oliver_engineer: started the replay job (job-id rpl-176953-01). will post logs when finished. provisional ETA ~45m.
\maria_support: keeping customer updated. they appreciate the pin. :thumbsup:
emma_support: please also capture whether fallback causes memory growth on the instance (we saw OOM risk in previous kernel_fallback cases).
oliver_engineer: noted, enabling mem profiling. will attach heap dumps if we hit OOM.
jasper_oncall: follow-up actions: 1) Oliver reproduce + logs, 2) Research collect kernel traces, 3) Release decide on patch/rollback, 4) Keep customer pinned until proven fixed. tagging @eng-runtime and @eng-ml for visibility.
emma_support: will file postmortem template after root cause. thanks everyone.
